column1: # Proto-Germanic, as reconstructed for roughly 500 BCE.
# þ = θ, h = x, ē₁ = æː, ē₂ = eː, ō = oː; b d g stand for [b~β d~ð g~ɣ].
# Nouns and adjectives are stems without the nominative ending (wulfa for
# *wulfaz); verbs are present stems (the infinitive without -an).
# Hand-written from Kroonen, Etymological Dictionary of Proto-Germanic
# (2013) and Ringe, From Proto-Indo-European to Proto-Germanic (2006).
# Concepts left out are coined in Proto-Germanic's own sounds.

column2: The ancestor of the Germanic languages, after Grimm's and Verner's laws: fixed initial stress, a dental past tense.
Kroonen, Etymological Dictionary of Proto-Germanic (2013); Ringe (2006) — simplified by hand
